title: Dawn bridge — morning on-call roundup + action items (EU)
content:
OVERVIEW:

Dawn bridge summary for EU morning shift (2026-04-06). Short night: two small incidents, one long-running degradation trace we should follow up on. This is lighter than last week but includes a couple of persistent flakes around prefix-cache eviction and our internal model-mirroring job. Handing over to day team with action items and a runbook draft that needs review.

KEY METRICS / OBSERVATIONS (from 00:00 - 06:00 UTC):
- 99th p95 latency for text-gen infra spiked to ~420ms at 03:12 UTC for ~12m; baseline ~300ms.
- Error rate (5xx) on hosted-api route /v1/generate peaked 0.9% (avg 0.05%).
- Autoscaler activity: 2 scale-out events triggered for dedicated-pool-eu-west-3 between 02:30-03:00 due to backlog.
- Request distribution shifted (short prompt burst from a new partner integration) — see linked analytics snapshot.

INCIDENTS (summary):
1) INC-2026-04-06-1: transient prefix-cache lock contention
   - Time: 03:05 - 03:20 UTC
   - Impact: increased token latency on a subset of requests served from cached KV shards; manifest as backend queueing and delayed KV fetches.
   - Mitigation applied: temporarily increased cache-concurrency knob on runtime (runtime flag: kv_cache.parallel_reads=8 -> 12) and rolled forward a hotfix on 3 nodes.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: race in cache invalidation path when parallel requests try to rehydrate same prefix simultaneously; appears correlated with model-mirroring job churn.
   - Owner: Miles Chen (ongoing follow-up).

2) SRE-4821: model-mirroring job failures (intermittent)
   - Time: recurring, observed during night window (02:00 - 05:30 UTC)
   - Impact: delayed mirror of newly onboarded model artifacts to dedicated pools; no direct customer-visible errors but increased fullness of staging buckets which may influence routing decisions.
   - Temporary workaround: retries backoff increased and queue depth reduced via admin UI.
   - Action: schedule deeper investigation; possibility of S3 transient 5xxs combined with insufficient retries.
   - Owner: Tomás Alvarez.

OTHER NOTES / SMALL GRIPES:
- A single 504 from an internal healthcheck probe (svc-prov-redis) at 04:45 UTC — flapped back within 90s; likely noisy neighbor on infra node. Logged ticket to infra pool owners.
- Observability note: spans for kv-cache ops are missing a custom tag (cache.shard_id) in some traces; makes correlation harder. Filing small instrumentation PR.

ACTIONS IN PROGRESS (what I've started and you can pick up):
- Miles restarted two runtime replicas with patched kv locks. Logs under GHPR #2870 include side-by-side traces.
- I created a runbook draft section (see "Runbook draft" below) and opened a PR to add a safeguard to prefix invalidation paths.
- Increased retry/backoff on model-mirroring — needs longer run to validate.

PRIORITY FOLLOW-UPS (owners and deadlines):
- Add shard_id tracing to kv-cache spans (low friction). Owner: Sara Gomez. ETA: 2026-04-08.
- Deep-dive on prefix-cache race (postmortem draft). Owner: Miles Chen. ETA: 2026-04-09 for initial notes.
- Expand model-mirroring retry logic and add circuit-breaker to prevent queue flooding. Owner: Tomás Alvarez. ETA: 2026-04-12.
- Review autoscaler policy thresholds for dedicated-pool-eu-west-3. Owner: eng-platform oncall rotation; ping @infra-owner.

RUNBOOK DRAFT (work-in-progress; please iterate):
Title: "Prefix cache contention — emergency mitigation steps"
Purpose: Short checklist to reduce customer impact and gather diagnostics when prefix cache lock contention is suspected.

Steps: (1) Identify hotspot
  - Query traces: trace tag kv.op=="rehydrate" and kv.lock_wait > 50ms.
  - Identify affected nodes: use runtime /nodes endpoint and grep for "lock_wait_count" metric.
(2) Reduce surface area
  - Toggle runtime flag for parallel reads: kv_cache.parallel_reads=8 -> 12 (see runtime flags doc).
  - If load persists, temporarily disable prefix prefetch for the affected model via model-config override.
(3) Restart strategy
  - Restart one replica at a time in failing AZ; wait 60s between restarts; verify queue depth returns to steady state.
(4) Collect diagnostics
  - Upload hot traces to S3 (path: s3://redwood-dumps/sre/2026-04-06/prefix-cache) and attach to Jira.
(5) Long-term actions
  - Add per-shard invalidation guard with exponential backoff on rehydration.

QUICK COMMANDS / DEBUG SNIPPETS (copy-paste friendly):
- Check runtime health via admin API: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://runtime-eu-west-3.internal/api/v1/nodes | jq '.[] | {id, lock_wait_count, queue_depth}'
- Tail logs for a node: gcloud compute ssh runtime-node-112 -- journalctl -u runtime -f | sed -n '1,200p'
- Trigger controlled restart (one replica): ./ops/restart-replica.sh --region eu-west-3 --replica-id runtime-112 --wait 60s

ESCALATION / CONTACTS (order):
1) Oncall infra lead (pager): Miles Chen — pager: +1-555-0102
2) Platform manager (Slack): @infra-owner (Sara Gomez)
3) Product-ops if customer-facing routing changes required: @linda-bae

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED:
- Should we make kv_cache.parallel_reads a dynamic config surfaced in the Console for Dedicated customers? (Pros: faster mitigation; Cons: more knobs exposed).
- Do we want an automated guard that stops model-mirroring when staging-bucket queue depth > X to avoid cascade? (suggested X=200)

HANDOFF CHECKLIST (for incoming day shift):
- [ ] Confirm prefix-cache contention has not recurred after 07:00 UTC.
- [ ] Follow-up with Miles for postmortem draft and link to Jira.
- [ ] Validate model-mirroring retries success metrics; ensure we have dampening of retries to avoid queue spamming.
- [ ] Merge shard_id tracing PR after quick review and monitor traces for a full 24h.

NOTABLE LINKS / ARTIFACTS:
- Incident ticket: INC-2026-04-06-1
- Postmortem placeholder: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-04-06-1
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2870
- Observability dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/sre/prefix-cache

FINAL COMMENTS: This was a manageable window but the prefix-cache race is subtle and will likely reappear if model-mirroring churn continues. Keep an eye on queue depth metrics and prioritize the tracing instrumentation (shard_id) — it will pay back immediately for debugging latency spikes.

-- Aisha (night bridge lead)
